ops.title: Three guards pin the MCP tool inventory, not two — redirect_inventory_test.go:71 machine-enforces CC_NOTES_TOOLS
ops.body:
## Correction

Planning material in this repo states that adding an MCP tool trips two
machine-enforced guards and that `CC_NOTES_TOOLS` in
`plugin/capt-hook/hooks/common.py` is hand-mirrored, so a new tool can silently
drop out of the hook pack's approval/redirect map.

**That is false.** There are three guards, and the third machine-enforces
`CC_NOTES_TOOLS` in both directions. It has existed since 2026-07-16.

| Guard | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `internal/mcpserver/inventory_test.go:121` `TestMCPVocabularyMatchesCobra` | every tool's synthesized argv is vocabulary the cobra tree accepts |
| `internal/mcpserver/reverse_test.go:231` `TestCobraReachableFromMCP` | every runnable CLI leaf and local flag is reachable from some MCP tool |
| `internal/mcpserver/redirect_inventory_test.go:71` `TestPackInventoryMatchesRegistry` | **`CC_NOTES_TOOLS` == the live MCP tool registry, both directions** |

The two-guard belief most likely comes from the third file's name: it reads as
"redirect" rather than "inventory", so a recon pass grepping for inventory-
shaped filenames misses it.

## How the third guard works

`inventoryToolSet` (redirect_inventory_test.go:25) reads
`plugin/capt-hook/hooks/common.py`, finds `CC_NOTES_TOOLS = frozenset(`, then
**brace-balances** from the following `{` to its matching `}` so it windows to
exactly that set literal — no other string literal in the module
(`CC_NOTES_EXECUTABLES`, `WRAPPER_EXECUTABLES`, shell-word sets) can leak in.
Inside that window it lifts every `"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)"` match; comments
in the block carry no quotes, so prose is never mistaken for a tool name.

The test then compares that set against `ListTools` over a live in-memory MCP
session built on the neutered cobra root, and errors per name in both
directions.

Introduced by 3e2753b (2026-07-16); retargeted from the old pack layout onto
`common.py` by 64417ec (2026-07-20).

## Proof, run 2026-07-26

Reverse direction — dropped `"task_renew"` from `CC_NOTES_TOOLS`:

```
--- FAIL: TestPackInventoryMatchesRegistry (0.20s)
    redirect_inventory_test.go:113: registered MCP tool "task_renew" is absent from plugin/capt-hook/hooks/common.py CC_NOTES_TOOLS
```

Forward direction — added a bogus `"task_teleport"`:

```
--- FAIL: TestPackInventoryMatchesRegistry (0.15s)
    redirect_inventory_test.go:101: plugin/capt-hook/hooks/common.py CC_NOTES_TOOLS names "task_teleport", which is not a registered MCP tool
```

## Consequence for anyone adding an MCP tool

Adding a tool turns `TestPackInventoryMatchesRegistry` red until its name is
added to `CC_NOTES_TOOLS`. That is the intended workflow, not a gap. Do not
build a `cc-notes mcp --list-tools` flag or a plugin-side Python equality test
to close it: the flag would have no consumer (STYLEGUIDE §1, §5), and a Python
test would duplicate a deterministic in-process Go test with one that depends
on a built binary — `capt-hook pack test plugin` runs in CI with no Go
toolchain.

Source-tree pinning is the correct granularity: the pack and the binary ship
from the same repo and the same release, so a stale binary against a newer pack
is a distribution problem a runtime probe would report but not fix.
